title: What Everest's summit does to your blood 🏔️
subject: everest
description:
Would you climb Everest without oxygen? 👇

What happens to your body at the top of Mount Everest? Near the summit, air pressure is about one third of sea level. In a 2009 study, doctors sampled arterial blood from 4 climbers at 8,400 meters and measured the lowest oxygen levels ever recorded in humans, levels seen at sea level only in patients close to death. National Geographic notes the human body can't stay indefinitely above 19,000 feet.

Sources: Grocott et al., New England Journal of Medicine (2009) "Arterial blood gases and oxygen content in climbers on Mount Everest", UCL News, ScienceDaily, Matthews et al., iScience (2019) via Live Science, National Geographic

scenes.text: On Everest, your blood looks like a dying patient's.
Near the top, the air pressure is about one third of sea level.
In one famous study, doctors drew blood from 4 climbers at 8,400 meters.
And here's the scary part. Their oxygen levels were the lowest ever recorded in humans.
At sea level, numbers that low are only seen in patients close to death.
Your body can't live for good above about 19,000 feet, and Everest's summit is over 29,000.
